architectures.name: Pressure-relief bypass (spring-loaded valve)
architectures.description: Spring-loaded bypass valve opens when dP > 15 mmHg, shunting CSF past membrane
architectures.drainage_preservation: YES — full shunt flow (0.35 mL/min) when bypass open
architectures.failure_of_failure: Redundant second spring; symptomatic headache if both fail
architectures.worst_case_behavior: Spring yields open → permanent bypass (drainage preserved, retention lost)

architectures.name: Membrane-bypass geometry (elastic slits)
architectures.description: Membrane sleeve has axial slits that open under high pressure
architectures.worst_case_behavior: Slits fail to open → ICP rises (symptomatic)

architectures.name: Redundant drainage channel (parallel path)
architectures.description: Second parallel drainage channel without membrane, normally restricted
architectures.trigger: dP > 20 mmHg (higher threshold — only for acute occlusion)
architectures.failure_of_failure: Two independent channels must both occlude for failure
architectures.worst_case_behavior: Both channels occlude → ICP rises (very unlikely)

architectures.name: Dissolvable plug (time-delayed backup)
architectures.description: Dissolvable plug in parallel channel opens after sustained ICP elevation
architectures.failure_mode: Plug dissolves prematurely or fails to dissolve
architectures.failure_of_failure: If plug fails, patient presents with acute hydrocephalus
architectures.modeled_safety_margin: FAIL for acute occlusion — 2-hour response too slow
architectures.safety_classification: UNACCEPTABLE_AS_PRIMARY — acceptable as tertiary backup only

selection.rationale: FS1 + FS3 provide redundant drainage preservation. FS4 is tertiary backup only (2-hour response too slow for acute).

engineering_gate.rationale: 3 acceptable fail-safe architectures (FS1, FS2, FS3) with drainage preservation. FS4 rejected as primary. Composite FS1+FS3 design provides redundancy.

honest_caveats: All response times are engineering estimates, not measured
Spring fatigue life requires accelerated aging testing
Elastomer creep (FS2) requires chronic material testing
Redundant channel (FS3) requires in vivo validation that independent fouling is achievable
